developerknowledge_answer_query.rationale: Pass-through (read-public): answers questions from Google's public product documentation. Never touches the user's project.

firebase_create_android_sha.rationale: Registers a signing certificate hash, admitting a new app build to the project's authenticated surface.

firebase_create_app.rationale: Creates a new client app registration in the active project.

firebase_create_project.rationale: Provisions a new billable Firebase project.

firebase_deploy.rationale: Deploys whatever firebase.json specifies — including Firestore and Storage security rules. One call can open a database to anonymous public access.

firebase_deploy_status.rationale: Pass-through (read): status of a background deployment job.

firebase_get_environment.rationale: Pass-through (metadata-only): current CLI environment and active project.

firebase_get_sdk_config.rationale: Pass-through (read): returns the client SDK config. The apiKey it contains is designed to ship inside client applications — a project identifier, not a secret — so this is not credential disclosure.

firebase_get_security_rules.rationale: Pass-through (read): reveals the project's security posture, but reading rules confers no ability to change them; firebase_deploy is the governed write path.

firebase_init.rationale: Initializes services in the workspace, writing configuration and provisioning databases.

firebase_login.rationale: Credential injection. Establishes a Google session sourced outside the Credential Adapter, so every later call runs under an identity the operator never provisioned.

firebase_logout.rationale: Ends the CLI session. Disruptive, but it terminates authority rather than establishing it, and is reversible.

firebase_update_environment.rationale: Re-targeting, and more. Switches the active project so later approved deploys land elsewhere, and can accept Terms of Service on the account owner's behalf.
